The Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) is constructed from Standard Model fields and must respect the fundamental symmetries of the Standard Model and of quantum field theory. Lorentz symmetry is a core requirement for any relativistic QFT. Poincaré symmetry, which includes Lorentz transformations and spacetime translations, is the full spacetime symmetry of the theory. While CP symmetry is violated in the Standard Model (and thus not required for all SMEFT operators), CPT symmetry is a fundamental consequence of Lorentz invariance, locality, and unitarity (the CPT theorem) and must be respected by all operators. Therefore, the symmetries that must be respected are Lorentz, Poincaré, and CPT.

Answer: A
